impact_preconditions: A caller invokes a public lower-layer ACK API with an invalid nonzero security fact, demonstrated with integer 2.
The store currently offers the same session/sequence; the IDF packet additionally has valid AK header, reserved byte, length and CRC.
Original code writes the persistent ACK marker. Reopening no longer offers that record.
A separate legitimate safe_idle=1 maintenance request may then reclaim the now-marked-ACKed log. ACK itself does not erase.

entries.change: authenticated_peer must equal 1; all other integers return existing -3 before writes, syncs or offer/cursor mutation.
entries.preserved: Exact offered session/seq, CRC-bound ACK body, ACK commit marker, two synchronization points and error latch.
entries.test: Invalid signed values over -255..255 excluding 1 plus INT_MIN/INT_MAX and +/-65536; rejection retains media and replay across reopen, legitimate later ACK succeeds.

entries.change: Each of encrypted/authenticated/bonded/approved_peer must equal 1. They are caller-supplied connection facts, not fields read from the ACK packet.
entries.preserved: 20-byte AK version-1 packet, reserved=0, payload CRC, current offered identity and existing return codes.
entries.test: Each signed security parameter tested separately; malformed packet header/version/reserved/CRC/session/seq/length and disabled context rejected; valid retry and subsequent reclaim preserved.
entries.boundary: Actual adapter C compiled against host API doubles, not the ESP-IDF SDK or physical NVS/Flash.

entries.change: None. Existing application route already requires all four current/receipt uint8_t facts exactly 1, nonzero matching epochs and the accepted-send ticket.
entries.test: 2040 malformed current/receipt boolean cases plus zero/stale/mismatched epoch cases rejected on original and candidate; legitimate retry succeeds.

failure_model: Four ACK program/sync failure points checked. A final-sync error is an uncertain outcome: in the synchronous memory fixture a complete authorized ACK marker is already durable and is recognized after reopen. Earlier failures retain replay and allow retry. No stronger physical persistence claim is made.
limitations: No demonstrated remote exploit, current-actor bypass or physical data loss. Correctly sourced authenticated link facts remain required. A wrong fact already normalized to 1 is not detected by this domain check. Legacy low-layer API epoch/security provenance is not redesigned.
